concept_name: Fold on a Line of Symmetry

item.question: Prem wants to cut out the letter M from a folded paper. Which fold should Prem use, and how much of the M must be drawn?
steps: Look at the M. The left side and the right side match, so the M has a vertical line of symmetry.
Fold the paper in half along the vertical line.
Draw half of the M, which is 1/2 of the letter, along the fold.
Cut along the outline and open the paper: the full M appears.
Check: the top and the bottom of the M do not match, so it has no horizontal line. One fold is all that works, and a quarter is not enough.
item.answer: Fold the paper in half along the vertical line and draw 1/2 of the M

concept_name: Horizontal and Vertical Lines of Symmetry

item.question: Which lines of symmetry do the letters B, W and H have?
steps: B: fold along a vertical line. The left side is straight and the right side has two bumps, so the halves do not match. Fold along a horizontal line. The top bump lands on the bottom bump, so the halves match. B has a horizontal line only.
W: fold along a vertical line. The left half lands on the right half, so they match. Fold along a horizontal line. The top and the bottom do not match. W has a vertical line only.
H: fold along a vertical line and the halves match. Fold along a horizontal line and the halves match. H has both lines.
Check: only H has two lines, so only H needs a quarter fold.
item.answer: B: horizontal line only. W: vertical line only. H: both lines
item.text:
Worked example: Which lines of symmetry do the letters B, W and H have?
1. B: fold along a vertical line. The left side is straight and the right side has two bumps, so the halves do not match. Fold along a horizontal line. The top bump lands on the bottom bump, so the halves match. B has a horizontal line only.
2. W: fold along a vertical line. The left half lands on the right half, so they match. Fold along a horizontal line. The top and the bottom do not match. W has a vertical line only.
3. H: fold along a vertical line and the halves match. Fold along a horizontal line and the halves match. H has both lines.
4. Check: only H has two lines, so only H needs a quarter fold.
Answer: B: horizontal line only. W: vertical line only. H: both lines

item.question: A paper pinwheel has 4 blades and a dot on the top blade. Turn it to the right, the same way each time. Where is the dot after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn and a 3/4 turn?
steps: A full turn is 4 quarter turns, so each quarter turn moves the dot on by one blade.
After a 1/4 turn the dot moves from the top blade to the right blade.
After a second quarter turn the dot is on the bottom blade. Two quarter turns make a 1/2 turn, because 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.
After a third quarter turn the dot is on the left blade. Three quarter turns make a 3/4 turn.
After the fourth quarter turn the dot is back on the top blade, where it started: a full turn.
Check: 1/4 turn, right blade; 1/2 turn, bottom blade; 3/4 turn, left blade; full turn, top blade.
item.answer: After a 1/4 turn the dot is on the right blade, after a 1/2 turn on the bottom blade, and after a 3/4 turn on the left blade
item.text:

2. After a 1/4 turn the dot moves from the top blade to the right blade.
3. After a second quarter turn the dot is on the bottom blade. Two quarter turns make a 1/2 turn, because 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.
4. After a third quarter turn the dot is on the left blade. Three quarter turns make a 3/4 turn.
5. After the fourth quarter turn the dot is back on the top blade, where it started: a full turn.
6. Check: 1/4 turn, right blade; 1/2 turn, bottom blade; 3/4 turn, left blade; full turn, top blade.
Answer: After a 1/4 turn the dot is on the right blade, after a 1/2 turn on the bottom blade, and after a 3/4 turn on the left blade

concept_name: Rotational Symmetry: Looks the Same After a Turn

item.question: Does the letter Z have rotational symmetry? Does the letter T? Turn each one by 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.
steps: Z: put a dot on the top left of the Z.
After a 1/4 turn the Z lies on its side and looks like an N, so it does not look the same.
After a 1/2 turn the Z is upside down and looks the same, with the dot now at the bottom right.
After a 3/4 turn the Z lies on its other side and looks like an N again, so it does not look the same.
The Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so it has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn.

T: after a 1/4 turn the T lies on its side. After a 1/2 turn it is upside down, with the bar at the bottom. After a 3/4 turn it lies on its other side. None of these looks like the T, so the T has no rotational symmetry.
Check: every shape looks the same after a full turn, so the full turn does not count.
item.answer: The Z has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. The T has no rotational symmetry
item.text:

2. After a 1/4 turn the Z lies on its side and looks like an N, so it does not look the same.
3. After a 1/2 turn the Z is upside down and looks the same, with the dot now at the bottom right.
4. After a 3/4 turn the Z lies on its other side and looks like an N again, so it does not look the same.
5. The Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so it has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn.
6. T: after a 1/4 turn the T lies on its side. After a 1/2 turn it is upside down, with the bar at the bottom. After a 3/4 turn it lies on its other side. None of these looks like the T, so the T has no rotational symmetry.
7. Check: every shape looks the same after a full turn, so the full turn does not count.
Answer: The Z has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. The T has no rotational symmetry

steps_tex: (a): the I is a straight bar. After a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn it lies flat, so it does not look the same. After a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn it looks the same. After a $\frac{3}{4}$ turn it lies flat again. After a full turn it looks the same. Rotational symmetry: yes, at $\frac{1}{2}$ turn.
(b): the X looks the same after a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn, after a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn, after a $\frac{3}{4}$ turn and after a full turn. Rotational symmetry: yes, at $\frac{1}{4}$ turn.

(c): the Y lies on its side after a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn, is upside down after a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn and lies on its other side after a $\frac{3}{4}$ turn. None of these looks the same, only the full turn does. Rotational symmetry: no.
Check: only a turn smaller than a full turn counts, so the Y has no rotational symmetry.

concept_name: Reflection Only, Turn Only or Both

item.question: Sort the letter M, the letter S and the plus sign into: reflection symmetry only, rotational symmetry only, both symmetries, or neither.
steps: M, Test 1: it has a vertical line of symmetry. Test 2: after a 1/2 turn it looks like a W, so it does not look the same. M has reflection symmetry only.

S, Test 1: fold it along a vertical line or a horizontal line and the halves do not match, so there is no line of symmetry. Test 2: after a 1/2 turn the S looks the same. S has rotational symmetry only.
The plus sign, Test 1: it has a vertical line and a horizontal line. Test 2: it looks the same after a 1/4 turn. It has both symmetries.
Check: each of the three signs went to a different group.
item.answer: M: reflection symmetry only. S: rotational symmetry only. The plus sign: both

item.question: Now, let us look at the following numbers: 11 and 1001. Do these have rotational symmetry, reflection symmetry or both symmetries?
steps_tex: The digit $1$ is drawn as a plain bar. Test each number with a fold line and with a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn.
$11$: fold along the vertical line between the two bars and the halves match. Turn it a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn: the two bars swap places and the number looks the same.

$1001$: fold along the vertical line between the two zeros and the halves match. Turn it a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn: the first $1$ lands at the end, the last $1$ lands at the start, and each $0$ still looks like a $0$, so the number looks the same.
So $11$ and $1001$ both have reflection symmetry and rotational symmetry.

concept_name: A Design That Looks the Same After a Turn

item.question: A design has a circle in the middle and one triangle above it, pointing up. Add triangles so that the design looks the same after a 1/2 turn, and then after a 1/4 turn.
steps: After a 1/2 turn the top triangle lands at the bottom, pointing down. Add a triangle below the circle, pointing down.
Now the design has 1 + 1 = 2 triangles, and it looks the same after a 1/2 turn.
After a 1/4 turn the top triangle lands on the right, pointing right, and the bottom triangle lands on the left, pointing left. Add a triangle on the right and one on the left.
Now the design has 2 + 2 = 4 triangles, one on each side of the circle.
The design looks the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn: 4 times in a full turn.
Check: after a 1/4 turn each triangle lands on the place of the next triangle.
item.answer: Add a triangle below the circle for a 1/2 turn, then a triangle on the left and on the right for a 1/4 turn

5. The design looks the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn: 4 times in a full turn.
6. Check: after a 1/4 turn each triangle lands on the place of the next triangle.

concept_name: Turn Symmetry and Reflection Symmetry in a Design

item.question: A square is cut by its two diagonals into 4 triangles. The top and bottom triangles are orange and the left and right triangles are blue. Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn? After a 1/4 turn? Find its lines of symmetry.
steps: Turn it a 1/2 turn: the top triangle lands on the bottom triangle, both orange, and the left triangle lands on the right triangle, both blue. It looks the same.
Turn it a 1/4 turn: the top triangle lands on the right triangle, orange on blue. It does not look the same.
Fold along the vertical line: the left triangle lands on the right triangle, blue on blue, and the top and bottom triangles each land on themselves. It is a line of symmetry.
Fold along the horizontal line: the top triangle lands on the bottom triangle, orange on orange. It is a line of symmetry.
Fold along a diagonal: the top triangle lands on the left triangle, orange on blue. It is not a line of symmetry.
Check: the design looks the same after a 1/2 turn, not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry.
item.answer: It looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry: the vertical line and the horizontal line
item.text:

3. Fold along the vertical line: the left triangle lands on the right triangle, blue on blue, and the top and bottom triangles each land on themselves. It is a line of symmetry.
4. Fold along the horizontal line: the top triangle lands on the bottom triangle, orange on orange. It is a line of symmetry.
5. Fold along a diagonal: the top triangle lands on the left triangle, orange on blue. It is not a line of symmetry.
6. Check: the design looks the same after a 1/2 turn, not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry.
Answer: It looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry: the vertical line and the horizontal line
